nodes.summary: The feasible region of a linear program with $m$ variables, constraint matrix $A$ and right-hand side $b$ is the set of vectors $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$ with $A x \le b$ and $x \ge 0$, both inequalities holding componentwise. It is a convex polyhedron in $\mathbb{R}^m$.
nodes.title: Feasible region of a linear program

nodes.summary: A linear program in standard inequality form with $m$ variables and $n$ constraints is given by an objective vector $c \in \mathbb{R}^m$, a right-hand side $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and an $n \times m$ real constraint matrix $A$; it stands for the problem of maximising $c \cdot x$ over $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$ subject to $A x \le b$ and $x \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Linear program

nodes.summary: Consider a linear program with $m$ variables and objective vector $c \in \mathbb{R}^m$, let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ be its feasible region and $f(x) = c \cdot x$ its objective function, and let $x \in P$ be a local maximiser of $f$ on $P$, that is, $f(y) \le f(x)$ for all $y \in P$ in some neighbourhood of $x$. nodes.title: Maximum principle for linear programming

nodes.summary: The objective function of a linear program with $m$ variables and objective vector $c \in \mathbb{R}^m$ is the map $f \colon \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}$ given by $f(x) = c \cdot x = \sum_i c_i x_i$.
nodes.title: Objective function of a linear program

nodes.summary: Consider a linear program with $m$ variables and objective vector $c \in \mathbb{R}^m$, and let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ be its feasible region and $f(x) = c \cdot x$ its objective function. If $P$ is nonempty and bounded, then some $x \in P$ maximises $f$ on $P$ and is an extreme point of $P$, that is, $x$ does not lie in the open segment between two distinct points of $P$.
nodes.title: Optimal vertices of linear programs

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
